title: PRD: Staged rollback & kernel-regression circuit-breaker safety contracts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Update the serving PRD to convert incident action items from the Jan 28 KV-regeneration postmortem into concrete safety contracts: implement a kernel-regression circuit-breaker, define staged rollback triggers and verification gates, and add synthetic acceptance tests that run during canary and rollout windows.
background: During the 2026-01-28 incident a regression in a compiled attention kernel caused elevated tail latency and bursty KV-cache invalidations. The postmortem recommended engineered safety contracts that couple runtime monitoring with automated staged rollback and stronger acceptance checks. This PRD update translates those actions into product requirements and measurable acceptance criteria for runtime-1.25.
goals: Define a kernel-regression circuit-breaker that can automatically quiesce affected binary kernels and route to a verified fallback path
Specify staged rollback policies with explicit canary evaluation windows and automated verification gates tied to synthetic workloads
Add acceptance tests (synthetic + smoke) that detect performance regressions and model-output drift before rollout completion
Ensure operational runbooks and SLA-preserving fallback behaviors are codified and instrumented in the Console
non_goals: Implement new kernel compilation toolchain (this PRD defines contracts only, engineering will propose toolchain changes separately)
Replace KV cache design: we assume current KV cache behavior and add guards rather than redesign cache semantics
requirements: R1: Circuit-breaker service that monitors kernel-level telemetry (per-kernel tail latency, error rate, memory spikes) and exposes an API to mark a kernel as 'throttled' for routing decisions
R2: Routing policy support to route traffic away from servers using throttled kernels to pre-warmed fallback workers running a verified kernel build
R3: Staged rollback workflow: canary window (15 minutes default), automatic mid-canary abort if any gate fails, progressive percentage ramp-down rules

R4: Synthetic acceptance suite that runs during canary and requires: tail latency p99 <= baseline + 20%, throughput within 85% of baseline, and embedding-similarity drift < 0.02 (cosine) on a seeded prompt set
R5: Runbook toggles in Console to allow on-call to force an immediate rollback, force a kernel bypass, or mark an incident as mitigated with audit trail
R6: Telemetry dashboards and alerts: per-kernel SLOs, regression-detection alerts, and automatic annotated timeline events for rollouts
R7: Test harness to replay production KV-cache regeneration patterns in staging to validate fallback paths
R8: Backwards compatibility: circuit-breaker must default to disabled for older dedicated/private deployments unless explicitly enabled by customers
R9: Documentation: PRD must link to runbooks, escalation paths, and postmortem templates; Console UX changes must include help text and brief tutorials
acceptance_criteria: AC1: In staging, introducing a synthetic kernel regression (injecting a controlled latency penalty) must trigger the circuit-breaker within 3 minutes and route 100% of new requests to the fallback kernel within 5 minutes
AC2: During a canary rollout of runtime-1.25, the synthetic acceptance suite must pass across 5 consecutive canary windows; a single gate failure causes automatic abort
AC3: Console shows annotated rollback events and provides a one-click rollback that completes within target window documented in runbook
AC4: Post-deploy regression detection alert fires and creates an incident ticket automatically with diagnostic artifacts attached (kernel metrics, sample traces, and affected request IDs)
AC5: Customers on Dedicated/Private receive a UI toggle and API flag; feature defaults off and enabling requires explicit opt-in plus a notice in release notes
AC6: End-to-end test that replays a recorded KV-cache regeneration pattern completes without data corruption and latency SLOs are preserved for >=95% of requests
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal staging validation (eng + reliability): run synthetic regressions and iterate
Phase 1: Canary on 2% of hostnames with synthetic acceptance suite active for 30 minutes per cohort
Phase 2: Progressive ramp to 25% with additional automated checks and manual on-call sign-off
Phase 3: Full rollout conditional on 24h of stable telemetry and no automatic gate failures
Emergency: rollback can be triggered automatically by gates or manually via Console one-click rollback
implementation_notes: Work will coordinate across ENG-serving, ENG-infra, and Reliability teams. ENG owners must expose kernel-level metrics via the metric-exporter interface (ENG-8872)
Circuit-breaker should integrate with existing routing layer; prefer feature-flagged rollout to avoid impacting Dedicated/Private customers unless opted-in
Synthetic suite will live as part of the continuous gating pipeline and also be executable on-demand by on-call
Define a minimal schema for 'rollback event' that includes commit IDs, kernel build IDs, canary cohort, and linked traces for traceability
metrics: Request routing split percent to fallback kernel
Number of automatic rollbacks triggered by circuit-breaker
Synthetic acceptance pass rate across canary windows
Customer-facing latency SLO compliance (percent requests meeting SLO)
risks_mitigation: Risk: false positives from circuit-breaker cause unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: require corroboration from two independent signals (latency + error rate) before auto-abort
Risk: fallback kernel has lower quality outputs. Mitigation: include embedding-similarity checks and disable automatic fallback for high-quality-sensitive routes unless manually approved
Risk: Dedicated/Private customers unexpectedly affected. Mitigation: default-off opt-in, clear release notes, and migration guide
decisions: D1: Use a two-signal rule (latency spike + increased error rate) as the default circuit-breaker trigger
D2: Synthetic acceptance suite is required for canary completion; manual overrides must be logged and justified
D3: Fallback path will be a verified kernel build stored in the artifact registry rather than a live recompile
open_questions: Q1: What is the minimum number of requests in a canary window required to consider embedding-drift meaningful? (engineering proposal due from ENG-metrics)
Q2: Should regressions discovered in low-traffic regions use a longer canary window or regional auto-abort?
Q3: How will this interact with existing autoscaling policies for Dedicated—we need SRE guidance
